precepts.text: Six: Massah and Meribah. Chide means to be contentious, to go back and forth. They were almost ready to stone Moses over water, and the place was named for the chiding of the children of Israel, because they tempted the Lord, saying, Is the Lord among us, or not?
precepts.point: Because all those men which have seen my glory and my miracles have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice. Write the ten down; the Most High deals in numbers, and nothing in the Bible is insignificant.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Number six is at Massah and Meribah. “Wherefore the people did chide with Moses, and said, Give us water that we may drink.” To chide means to murmur, to be contentious, to go back and forth. “And Moses said unto them, Why chide ye with me? wherefore do ye tempt the Lord?”

Then, “the people murmured against Moses, and said, Wherefore is this that thou hast brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst? And Moses cried unto the Lord, saying, What shall I do unto this people? they be almost ready to stone me.” They were almost ready to stone the man who brought them out of Egypt, over water.

The Lord said, “Behold, I will stand before thee there upon the rock in Horeb; and thou shalt smite the rock, and there shall come water out of it, that the people may drink.” And Moses “called the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because of the chiding of the children of Israel, and because they tempted the Lord, saying, Is the Lord among us, or not?”

That is the very word Numbers 14:22 uses: they have “tempted me now these ten times.” The place itself was named for it.

precepts.text: Timna bare to Eliphaz Amalek; Amalek is the grandson of Esau, a duke of Edom.
precepts.point: The sign shewed the people whose hand their life was in: Moses is the man to hearken to, so do not speak against him. And Joshua discomfited Amalek with the edge of the sword; Joshua was a mighty warrior even then.

note.label: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek

precepts.why:
“Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim.” Amalek was the first nation to come against Israel after Egypt, and Amalek was of Esau. “And Timna was concubine to Eliphaz Esau’s son; and she bare to Eliphaz Amalek”. Amalek was born to Eliphaz of Timna the concubine; he is Esau's grandson, a duke in the land of Edom.

So the first war Israel fought out of Egypt was with the seed of Esau. Joshua discomfited Amalek with the edge of the sword while Moses held up his hand, and the sign shewed the people whose hand their life was in.

precepts.text: Remember what Amalek did, how he smote the hindmost, the feeble, the faint and weary, and feared not God; thou shalt blot out his remembrance.
precepts.point: The enmity was set from the garden between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed. They bruised Christ's heel, but at the end of the world Jacob bruises the head: the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly.

note.label: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek

precepts.why:
“Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua”. Moses wrote it, and Deuteronomy 25 is that rehearsal: “Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way, when ye were come forth out of Egypt; How he met thee by the way, and smote the hindmost of thee, even all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary; and he feared not God.”

Amalek did not meet the mighty men in the front. He went to the back, to smite the hindmost, all that were feeble, when Israel was faint and weary: the women, the children and the old ones. And he feared not God. That same spirit works against the nation's young and old today.

“Therefore it shall be, when the Lord thy God hath given thee rest from all thine enemies round about, in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee for an inheritance to possess it, that thou shalt blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven; thou shalt not forget it.” That is the “I will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven” of Exodus, rehearsed forty years later. By then the children of Amalek had done nothing themselves, and the charge still stood: the judgment carries to the seed.

precepts.text: Hundreds of years later the Lord remembered what Amalek did to Israel in the way from Egypt and sent Saul to destroy Amalek utterly.
precepts.point: The enmity was set from the garden between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed. They bruised Christ's heel, but at the end of the world Jacob bruises the head: the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly.

note.label: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek

precepts.why:
“the Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.” Hundreds of years after Moses, the Lord sent Saul by Samuel to keep that oath: “Thus saith the Lord of hosts, I remember that which Amalek did to Israel, how he laid wait for him in the way, when he came up from Egypt. Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not; but slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass.”

The Lord remembered what Amalek did coming out of Egypt, and the Amalekites of Saul's day, who had not been there, were to be utterly destroyed for it, man and woman, infant and suckling. God be true and every man a liar: the nations do not get away with what they did to His people, and the judgment carries to the seed.

Saul did not finish Agag's line, and in Esther's day Haman the Agagite, of that same seed, rose against Israel. The war truly runs from generation to generation.

precepts.text: Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers; the name and remnant are cut off, so none escape by saying it was only the forefathers.
precepts.point: The enmity was set from the garden between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed. They bruised Christ's heel, but at the end of the world Jacob bruises the head: the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly.

note.label: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek

precepts.why:
War with Amalek from generation to generation means the children answer for the fathers. “Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers; that they do not rise, nor possess the land, nor fill the face of the world with cities. For I will rise up against them, saith the Lord of hosts, and cut off from Babylon the name, and remnant, and son, and nephew, saith the Lord.”

The name, the remnant, the son and the nephew are cut off, so none escape by saying it was only the forefathers. Forty years after Rephidim the children of Amalek had done nothing themselves and were still marked; hundreds of years later Saul was sent against their seed. The nations do not get away with what they did to His people, and the judgment carries to the seed until the remembrance is put out from under heaven.

precepts.text: The blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan; the Most High knows the lie, and Israel in tribulation and poverty is rich.
precepts.point: The enmity was set from the garden between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed. They bruised Christ's heel, but at the end of the world Jacob bruises the head: the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly.

note.label: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek

precepts.why:
That seed is still here, and today it says it is Israel. Christ says, “I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich) and I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.”

They say they are Jews and are not; they are the synagogue of Satan, robbing Israel of identity and prospering off the oppression. The Most High knows the lie. And Israel in tribulation and poverty is rich: the true Jews are the ones with the tribulation and the poverty, and the ones with the name and the wealth are the blasphemers. This is Amalek's war from generation to generation, fought now with a stolen name.

precepts.text: The synagogue of Satan will be made to come and worship before Israel's feet, and to know that the Most High loved Israel.
precepts.point: The enmity was set from the garden between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed. They bruised Christ's heel, but at the end of the world Jacob bruises the head: the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly.

note.label: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek

precepts.why:
The Lord's war with Amalek ends with the seed brought low before Israel. “Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee.”

The ones who say they are Jews and are not, but do lie, will be made to come and worship before Israel's feet, and to know that the Most High loved Israel. The seed that robbed Israel of identity and prospered off the oppression will come to Israel's feet knowing who was loved. That is how the remembrance of Amalek is put out from under heaven.

precepts.text: Jacob's hand held first the heel of Esau; for Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.
precepts.point: The enmity was set from the garden between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed. They bruised Christ's heel, but at the end of the world Jacob bruises the head: the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly.

note.label: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek

precepts.why:
The war from generation to generation is the whole world's story. Esdras asked, “What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth? And he said unto me, From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau. For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.”

The whole world is set up between Jacob and Esau. Esau is the end of this world, the so-called white man, with Amalek leading, and Jacob is the beginning of the world that follows. The Lord's war with Amalek runs the length of this world, from Rephidim to Esau's end.

It is not speaking of the Arab man. If Ishmael had a rulership still to come, Israel would have another captivity to enter, and Christ has already redeemed us from the curse of the law.

precepts.text: Nothing stands between the heel and the hand; the world passes straight from Esau's end to Jacob's beginning.
precepts.point: The enmity was set from the garden between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed. They bruised Christ's heel, but at the end of the world Jacob bruises the head: the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly.

note.label: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek

precepts.why:
“The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand: other question, Esdras, ask thou not.” Jacob's hand held the heel of Esau, and nothing stands between the heel and the hand. The world passes straight from Esau's end to Jacob's beginning.

That is why it is not the Arab man. If Ishmael had a rulership still to come between Esau and Jacob, Israel would have another captivity to enter, and Christ has already redeemed us from the curse of the law. Esau is the end of this world, with Amalek leading, and the Lord's war with Amalek from generation to generation runs right up to Jacob's beginning, with nothing in between.

precepts.text: Enmity is set between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed; the battle between Esau's seed and Israel stands until the end.
precepts.point: The enmity was set from the garden between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed. They bruised Christ's heel, but at the end of the world Jacob bruises the head: the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly.

note.label: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek

precepts.why:
The war with Amalek from generation to generation is older than Amalek. In the garden the Lord said, “And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.” The enmity was set between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed from the beginning.

The battle between Esau's seed and Israel is that enmity, and it stands until the end. They bruised Christ's heel. But the head is bruised at the end of the world, and it is Jacob who bruises it. What Amalek began against the feeble and the weary coming out of Egypt is the serpent's seed against the woman's seed, and it ends the way the garden said it would.

precepts.text: The God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly; Jacob bruises the head at the end of the world.
precepts.point: The enmity was set from the garden between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed. They bruised Christ's heel, but at the end of the world Jacob bruises the head: the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly.

note.label: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek

precepts.why:
“And the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly.” The enmity set in the garden ends here: Satan bruised under the feet of Israel. They bruised Christ's heel; at the end of the world Jacob bruises the head.

That is the end of the Lord's war with Amalek from generation to generation. The seed that smote the hindmost coming out of Egypt, that rose again in Haman, that says it is Jews and is not, is made to come and worship before Israel's feet, and the God of peace bruises Satan under those same feet shortly.

precepts.text: When Moses held up his hand Israel prevailed, and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands until the going down of the sun.
precepts.point: The Most High chose able men. In the book of Judges He cut the army down from the thousands to three hundred; and when Moses held up his hands over the battle, mighty men had to hold his arms up.

note.label: Numbers 1: The Numbering of the Armies of Israel

precepts.why:
The armies numbered here were the men able to go forth to war, and the Most High chose able men. When Moses held up his hands over the battle, mighty men had to hold his arms up.

“And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed: and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.” When his hands grew heavy “they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat thereon; and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun.”

That is the kind of able men the Lord numbered by their armies: men who could stand with the man of God the whole day until the battle was won.

precepts.text: Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim; that is why Amalek is called the first of the nations.
precepts.point: His latter end shall be that he perish for ever; precept upon precept, the scriptures show who Amalek is and what his end is.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
“Amalek was the first of the nations.” That means Amalek was the first of the nations to come out and fight against Israel: “Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim.”

He met us at Rephidim as we came out of Egypt, before any other nation lifted a hand against Israel; that is why Amalek is called the first of the nations.

precepts.text: The remembrance of Amalek shall be utterly put out from under heaven, for the Lord hath sworn to have war with Amalek from generation to generation.
precepts.point: His latter end shall be that he perish for ever; precept upon precept, the scriptures show who Amalek is and what his end is.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
“his latter end shall be that he perish for ever.” The Lord swore it at Rephidim: “Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: for I will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.” Moses built an altar and called it JEHOVAH-nissi, “Because the Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.”

Amalek is the seed of Esau through Eliphaz, and Amalek is the people who call themselves Jewish in the land of Israel today. The war that has never left that land since they entered it is the war the Lord swore to have with Amalek from generation to generation, and the prophecy that none shall remain of the house of Esau belongs to no other nation.

Precept upon precept, the scriptures show who Amalek is and what his end is: the remembrance of him utterly put out from under heaven, perishing for ever.

“And Moses built an altar, and called the name of it JEHOVAH–nissi: For he said, Because the Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.” The Lord hath sworn it, from generation to generation, and that war is still going on even to this day.

precepts.text: The place was called Massah, and Meribah, because of the chiding of the children of Israel.
precepts.point: At the golden calf, when Moses stood in the gate of the camp and said, Who is on the Lord's side? let him come unto me, only the sons of Levi gathered themselves unto him. They took every man his sword and did according to the word of Moses without hesitating, and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men. That is why the blessing says they saw not father or mother nor acknowledged their brethren: that is the devotion they had for the covenant.

note.label: Deuteronomy 33: The Blessing of Moses, Identifying the Tribes in the Last Days

precepts.why:
Levi's holy one is the one “whom thou didst prove at Massah, and with whom thou didst strive at the waters of Meribah”. Exodus 17 names the place: “And he called the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because of the chiding of the children of Israel, and because they tempted the Lord, saying, Is the Lord among us, or not?”

Massah and Meribah were where the children of Israel chided and tempted the Lord, asking whether he was among them or not. That is the proving and the striving the blessing of Levi looks back to.

precepts.text: The Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation; that war did not end in the wilderness.
precepts.point: Christianity says forgive and forget, but the Most High God said remember; this is a righteous grudge, and it shows Leviticus 19:18 applies to the children of thy people.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

precepts.why:
“For he said, Because the Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.” That war did not end in the wilderness; it was still on in Saul’s day.

It applies to this day. The same war continues from generation to generation, and it is now more spiritual than ever, because the adversary has established the imagination that they are the Jews, and we go out and cast down that imagination every day.
